title: The new human-crafted Apple Music brand matters in an AI world
gist: Ars creative director Aurich Lawson argues that Apple's behind-the-scenes video for its new Apple Music brand shows why visible human craft will be valued more in an era of AI-generated imagery, as audiences grow suspicious of everything they see.

themes.theme: Human craft in the age of generative AI

insights.claim: Apple revealed a new Apple Music brand identity with a Liquid Glass look, produced with design agency TBWA/Media Arts Lab and producer Fred again.., using a mineral oil tank with a transducer to turn audio into physical ripples.
insights.speaker: Aurich Lawson
insights.so_what: Apple is using physical, process-visible production as brand positioning.
insights.locator: Let’s get the obvious part out of the way

insights.claim: The author argues people will increasingly value hands-on human craft and seeing the process behind it as anything can be generated from a prompt.
insights.speaker: Aurich Lawson
insights.so_what: Proof-of-human-process may become a premium differentiator in creative and brand work.
insights.quote: I see us increasingly place genuine value on not just human-created craft, but seeing the process behind it that shows the hands at work.
insights.locator: It’s a little eye-rolly with the narration

insights.claim: Ubiquitous generative AI imagery is creating a default suspicion about whether any image was hand-drawn or prompted using styles taken from human artists.
insights.speaker: Aurich Lawson
insights.so_what: Erosion of trust in visuals raises the value of provenance and authenticity signals.
insights.locator: One really unfortunate side effect of that persistence

insights.claim: Apple's video both promotes the brand and provides the receipts that real people did real things in the physical world to make the final images and videos.
insights.speaker: Aurich Lawson
insights.so_what: Showing the making-of is becoming a marketing tactic against AI-slop skepticism.
insights.locator: This Apple video was a neat bit of promotion

insights.claim: The author concludes generative AI is here to stay and that creators should celebrate human involvement and show behind-the-scenes process.
insights.speaker: Aurich Lawson
insights.so_what: Expect more brands to market human process as AI content proliferates.
insights.quote: There’s no stuffing the genie back in the bottle.
insights.locator: Generative AI is likely here to stay.

insights.claim: The author describes Apple as pretentious with all the resources of a $5 trillion market cap to bring to bear on every problem.
insights.speaker: Aurich Lawson
insights.so_what: Apple's market cap scale funds high-production brand work.
insights.locator: Let’s get the obvious part out of the way
